R4E-bear-drive-0001.name: By Birnam Creek
R4E-bear-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R4E-bear-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on Duncan-Glacier Creek FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2020 (6 years old), 220 m S: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2015 (fire N70653), 460 m NW: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 26 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Birnam Creek 50 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; private land only, with landowner permission

plan: Drive: from Village of Radium Hot Springs, about 82 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.34451, -116.84618, pull off on Duncan-Glacier Creek FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 250 m NW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 33 m, about 8 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-27, Region 4. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
R4E-bear-drive-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 4-27: about 96 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.06 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.2 km and about 33 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-4-001 unit 74 (official), 200 m NW. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), right here.
Burn from 2022 (fire N72255, 266 ha), 860 m E.
W facing slope, 31 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 2.0 km SE: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

R4E-deer-atv-0003.recDirections: From Kaslo BC Head North on Highway 31 for approximately 35 KM. just before Cooper Creek Turn right on Argenta Road.(you will see sign for Jumbo/Monica hiking trails just before the road). evidence.t: Road: Glacier Creek FSR, 3.8 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
2 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
24 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

flags.t: Route crosses private land (ParcelMap BC, updated 2026-10-01): get permission first or go around.
